title: Logitech G305 X SUPERLIGHT: What's New in the 59 g Wireless FPS Mouse?
summary: The Logitech G305 X SUPERLIGHT (2026) keeps the classic G305 shape but drops from 99 g to 59 g, swaps the AA battery for a USB-C rechargeable one, and adds Bluetooth and a HERO 44K sensor. In Asia it is sold as the G304 X SUPERLIGHT. The stock skates and a higher price than the old G305 are the most common complaints — is it worth buying?
description:
## Who is it for?

- FPS players who want a sub-60 g wireless mouse from a major brand.
- Claw and fingertip grippers with small to medium hands.
- G305/G304 owners who like the shape but are tired of AA batteries and 99 g.

## Why consider it?

- 59 g with the familiar G305 shape (Logitech).
- USB-C rechargeable battery rated at 130+ hours, plus tri-mode connectivity with Bluetooth.
- HERO 44K sensor, upgradable to 8,000 Hz with the PRO LIGHTSPEED receiver (sold separately).

sections.title: What is the Logitech G305 X SUPERLIGHT?
sections.content:
The G305 (G304 in Asia) has been one of Logitech's best-selling wireless gaming mice since 2018: a compact "egg" shape, a HERO sensor and a friendly price — but 99 g, because it runs on a AA battery. In June 2026 Logitech replaced it with the **G305 X SUPERLIGHT**, part of its G3 Series: the same shape, now **59 g**, with a USB-C rechargeable battery, Bluetooth and a HERO 44K sensor.

In Asian markets the same mouse is sold as the **G304 X SUPERLIGHT**; Alktech's review confirms it is the Asian variant with identical specs. Logitech's US store lists it at US$79.99 (November 2026), and launch pricing was £69.99 in the UK and €79.99 in Europe, according to KitGuru.

sections.title: Design: the familiar G305 shape at 59 g
sections.content:
It's a small, low, symmetrical mouse. Logitech's product page doesn't list dimensions; European retailers (LDLC, Arvutitark) give **117.3 × 63.9 × 38.2 mm** — close to the VXE R1 SE (about 120.6 × 64 × 37.8 mm). The shape suits claw and fingertip grips; Gamepadsquire notes it doesn't suit palm grips or large hands.

Logitech rates it at **59 g** (2.08 oz), while some retailers such as LDLC list 61 g. Either way, the drop from the old G305's 99 g is the headline change — PCGamesN calls it a massive reduction. There's a small LIGHTSYNC RGB strip, 6 buttons (two main clicks, two side buttons, the wheel click and a DPI button) and black, white and lilac colorways depending on region.

The most common complaint is the **stock skates**. PC Gamer says they add resistance and isn't a fan; Gamepadsquire finds them scratchy on cloth pads and suggests cheap aftermarket dot skates; Alktech also noticed extra friction and noise on a cloth pad, though it calls that a subjective preference.

sections.title: HERO 44K sensor, 1,000 Hz and the 8,000 Hz option
sections.content:
Logitech lists the HERO 44K sensor at up to **44,000 DPI**, 678+ IPS and 40+ G — flagship-class numbers, where the old G305 used the HERO 12K. Almost nobody plays at that DPI; the practical benefit is consistent tracking at any flick speed. TechRadar describes the mouse as impressively smooth and snappy.

Out of the box, the report rate is **1,000 Hz** both wireless and wired, according to Logitech's spec sheet. Logitech says it can be upgraded to **8,000 Hz** with the PRO LIGHTSPEED receiver (sold separately) — the included receiver stays at 1,000 Hz, and Gamepadsquire notes wired mode is also capped at 1,000 Hz. For most players 1,000 Hz is plenty, and 8,000 Hz drains the battery much faster.

Logitech doesn't specify the switches. Gamepadsquire lists Omron mechanical switches and praises the tight click tuning, while Truthful.reviews found the side buttons a little mushy. On the scroll wheel, Alktech found the steps distinct but Gamepadsquire found the detents less defined than expected — if wheel feel matters to you, try one in person.

sections.title: USB-C battery, Bluetooth and connectivity
sections.content:
The second big change from the old G305 is a **built-in rechargeable battery** instead of a AA cell. Logitech rates it at 130+ hours of constant motion, with 2 minutes of charging giving about 3.5 hours; Mediaberry reports battery life matched Logitech's claims in its testing. RGB and 8,000 Hz polling will shorten that. According to KitGuru and Gamepadsquire, the shell uses exposed screws and the battery is replaceable, which helps with repairs later on.

There are **three ways to connect**: the LIGHTSPEED 2.4 GHz USB-A receiver (lowest latency — use it for gaming), **Bluetooth** (new for the G305 line, handy for laptops and tablets) and a USB-C cable. What it **doesn't** have: Logitech doesn't list POWERPLAY wireless charging, the receiver is still USB-A rather than USB-C, and Gamepadsquire notes it won't track on glass.

sections.title: G305 X vs G304 X vs the original G305 — and similar mice
sections.content:
Several similar names are on sale, so check the exact model:

- **G305 X SUPERLIGHT / G304 X SUPERLIGHT** (this review, 2026): 59 g, USB-C rechargeable, Bluetooth, HERO 44K. G304 X is the Asian name; the specs are the same.
- **G305 / G304 LIGHTSPEED** (original, 2018): same shape but 99 g, AA battery, HERO 12K, no Bluetooth, no RGB. Cheaper — only worth it at a big discount if you don't mind the weight.
- **PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2**: Logitech's flagship esports mouse with a larger shape, also around 60 g but roughly twice the price. Don't confuse the two because of the shared "SUPERLIGHT" name.

Compared with mice we've covered:

- **VXE R1 SE / SE+** (about 51–55 g, tri-mode, PAW3395 SE sensor): lighter and much cheaper. The G305 X SUPERLIGHT wins on brand support, G HUB software, clearer warranty terms and the 8,000 Hz upgrade path.
- **Logitech G502 X LIGHTSPEED** (102 g, 13 programmable controls): better for MMOs/MOBAs and right-handed palm grips, but nearly twice the weight and no Bluetooth. For FPS, the G305 X SUPERLIGHT is the better fit.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content:
**Buy it if you:**
- Play FPS games (Valorant, CS2…) and want a sub-60 g wireless mouse from a major brand.
- Use a claw or fingertip grip with small to medium hands.
- Own an older G305/G304 and like the shape but not the AA battery and 99 g.
- Want one mouse for gaming (2.4 GHz) and for a laptop or tablet over Bluetooth.

**Skip it if you:**
- Have large hands and a palm grip — it will feel cramped.
- Need lots of buttons for MMOs or macros — look at the G502 X LIGHTSPEED.
- Want the lightest mouse for the least money — the VXE R1 SE costs far less.
- Don't want to buy replacement skates, or need 8,000 Hz without buying an extra receiver.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology **has not used** the Logitech G305 X SUPERLIGHT. This review is compiled and analyzed from: Logitech G's product pages (US and Singapore — sensor, report rate, buttons, battery, connectivity, US list price); KitGuru's launch report (release date, pricing, repairability); reviews by PCGamesN, PC Gamer, TechRadar, Gamepadsquire, Alktech (G304 X), Mediaberry and Truthful.reviews (weight, skates, switches, scroll wheel, battery); dimensions from retailer listings at LDLC and Arvutitark. Logitech does not publish dimensions or switch type, and reviewers disagree on the scroll wheel — both are noted above. Updated November 2026. Images are official Logitech G product photos.

sections.title: Is the Logitech G305 X SUPERLIGHT worth buying?
sections.content: The G305 X SUPERLIGHT fixes the two biggest weaknesses of the original G305: 99 g and a AA battery. At 59 g with USB-C charging, Bluetooth and a HERO 44K sensor, it's the best G305 yet and a strong pick for FPS players with small to medium hands who want a wireless mouse from a major brand. The trade-offs are mediocre stock skates, 1,000 Hz with the included receiver and a higher price than before. **Buy it at or below MSRP**; on a tight budget, the VXE R1 SE is lighter for a fraction of the price.

pros: Much lighter than the original G305: 59 g versus 99 g (Logitech).
USB-C rechargeable battery rated at 130+ hours; 2 minutes of charging gives about 3.5 hours — no more AA batteries.
Tri-mode connectivity: LIGHTSPEED 2.4 GHz for gaming, Bluetooth for laptops and tablets, plus USB-C wired.
HERO 44K sensor from Logitech's current generation, more than enough for any FPS.
Upgradable to 8,000 Hz with the PRO LIGHTSPEED receiver (sold separately).
Repair-friendly: exposed screws and a replaceable battery, per KitGuru and Gamepadsquire.
cons: Stock skates draw criticism from PC Gamer, Gamepadsquire and Alktech for friction on cloth pads — many owners swap them.
Costs US$20–30 more than the original G305, and several times more than budget ultralights like the VXE R1 SE.
Small shape doesn't suit large hands or palm grips.
Only 1,000 Hz with the included receiver; 8,000 Hz needs an extra receiver.
Just 6 buttons — far fewer than an MMO mouse like the G502 X LIGHTSPEED.
No POWERPLAY wireless charging, and the receiver is still USB-A (USB-C-only laptops need an adapter or Bluetooth).
buying_advice: Worth buying for FPS players with small to medium hands who want a light wireless mouse from a major brand, ideally at or below MSRP. On a tight budget, look at the VXE R1 SE; for lots of buttons, the G502 X LIGHTSPEED.

faq.question: What's the difference between the G305 X SUPERLIGHT and the G304 X SUPERLIGHT?
faq.answer: Essentially none. G304 X SUPERLIGHT is the name used in Asia and G305 X SUPERLIGHT in the US and Europe; the specs are the same and only the regional part numbers differ.

faq.question: How is it different from the original G305 LIGHTSPEED?
faq.answer: The X is much lighter (59 g vs 99 g), uses a USB-C rechargeable battery instead of a AA, adds Bluetooth and RGB, upgrades the sensor from HERO 12K to HERO 44K and supports 8,000 Hz with the optional PRO receiver. The shape is essentially unchanged.

faq.question: Does the G305 X SUPERLIGHT support 8,000 Hz?
faq.answer: Yes, but not out of the box. The included receiver runs at 1,000 Hz; 8,000 Hz requires the PRO LIGHTSPEED receiver, sold separately. Wired mode is also 1,000 Hz.

faq.question: Does it have Bluetooth?
faq.answer: Yes. It connects via the LIGHTSPEED 2.4 GHz receiver, Bluetooth or a USB-C cable. Use 2.4 GHz for gaming to get the lowest latency.

faq.question: How does it compare with the VXE R1 SE?
faq.answer: The Logitech has stronger brand support and clearer warranty terms, G HUB software, RGB and the 8,000 Hz upgrade path. The VXE R1 SE is lighter (about 51–55 g) and costs a fraction of the price.

faq.question: G305 X SUPERLIGHT or G502 X LIGHTSPEED?
faq.answer: For FPS with small to medium hands, choose the G305 X SUPERLIGHT (59 g, Bluetooth). For MMOs/MOBAs, lots of buttons and a right-handed palm grip, choose the G502 X LIGHTSPEED (102 g, 13 programmable controls).
